items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: such as the blues, Marlick Jazz, Rocky Roo.

ctx.x: I'm here. I'm here. I'm here. Okay. Well, now what should we talk about? Yeah, this is one thing which I'm interested in. It's very difficult to tell from just listening to records. Is whether the music, overall, the music, you think the music has changed over the years? The style. I mean, I'm talking just about the style. What you did. Dixon's. Well, not the Dixon language.

We had to change. It had to change. Not to my family. Yeah. Not the real old players have changed the style. No. But the young people have changed some of the styles of playing, such as the blues, Marlick Jazz, Rocky Roo.

Oh, yeah. Some other kind of a... But now, the thing is, if you listen to some of those old records, now this is what... I just have to go by the records, you see. But if you listen to those bands, now they only recorded a few of the bands down here, like, well, Louis Domaine, who was playing with, and Sam Morgan's band. Celestan. Celestan, yes. Celestan. Of course, the Perron Orchestra. Well, let's just take the Morgan band. To me, the Morgan band sounds to me like the style is nearly the same, but it's not…
